situational_context: Running comeback at 145 days (36 runs since May 3, 2026). C4 block (#21-40) lapsed — archive overdue (deadline was Sep 13), 12 km Beaumonts objective not attempted, block behind schedule. Gravel cycling resumed after 122-day hiatus: first ride Sep 15 (22.5 km), then a massive unplanned 49.6 km ride Sep 21 (load 145, D+ 416m, suffer 145) that spiked ACWR to ~2.18 — well above the 1.50 comeback ceiling. Four rest days since (Sep 22-25); recovery adequate: body battery 52, training readiness 67, RHR normalized to 54. Cold episode ('Gros rhume', severity 6) Sep 8-15, resolved. VO2max running 42.3 (stable); cycling corrected to 37.7 (artifact from prior Garmin sync resolved by gravel ride data). Weight 100.84 kg (Sep 23) — essentially flat on the 0.25 mg tolerability step; body composition favorable (fat 26.0 kg ↓, muscle 71.14 kg ↑ vs Sep 15). MEDICATION (standing, from protocols/health-profile.md): Benjamin is on Wegovy (semaglutide, GLP-1 receptor agonist) 0.25 mg weekly — first injection Wed 2026-08-12, injections every Wednesday (last Wed 2026-09-23; day 44 of therapy, day 44 on current dose). Follow-up consultation on 2026-09-15 confirmed: dose escalation to 0.5 mg on Wed 2026-09-30 (not Sep 9 as originally expected). Post-injection side-effect window today (Fri, J+2). Expected effects: RHR +1-5 bpm (observed +5.1 bpm vs pre-initiation 49.3; at upper edge), lower HRV (observed weekly avg 30, down from 36 pre-initiation — expected class effect), suppressed appetite, weight loss (modest at 0.25 mg). RHR/HRV read against post-initiation baseline; drift alone does not gate training (require second signal). Nutrition logging stopped 33 days ago (last log Aug 23) — protein floor and energy availability unverifiable; this is the P0 concern, distinct from the medication effect.

recommendations.text: Resume nutrition logging immediately. 33 consecutive days with zero intake recorded (last log Aug 23) while on Wegovy — the protein floor (160 g/day, 1.6 g/kg) and energy availability cannot be verified. On a GLP-1 agonist with suppressed appetite, this is not just a logging gap: it may mask genuine under-eating, which is the leading non-drug hypothesis for the chronically low body battery (avg 39.5) and HRV (avg 30). Even partial logging (one photo per meal) gives a signal. The dose escalation to 0.5 mg on Sep 30 will further suppress appetite — logging before the step establishes the current baseline.
recommendations.measurable: At least 3 of the next 7 days with non-zero calorie logging; protein >= 1.6 g/kg on every logged day

recommendations.text: Manage the 0.5 mg dose escalation (Sep 30). The follow-up consultation on Sep 15 confirmed stepping from 0.25 mg to 0.5 mg on the next Wednesday injection. Expect: increased GI side effects (nausea, reflux, early satiety) in the 14-day escalation watch window (Sep 30 - Oct 13); possible further RHR shift (+1-2 bpm); appetite suppression deepening. The RHR/HRV rebaseline clock restarts — do not compare post-step values to the current post-initiation baseline for 21 days. No key session in the post-injection window (Thu Oct 1 - Sat Oct 3); Oct 1 is already 'sur site'. Pre-hydrate more aggressively in the first week. Report any persistent nausea or GI distress to Dr Monnier.
recommendations.measurable: No GI-related training skip in the first 14 days; RHR/HRV recorded daily for rebaseline; Dr Monnier contacted if GI severity > 5/10 for 3+ days

recommendations.text: Archive the C4 block (#21-40) and plan the next training block. The block's archive deadline was Sep 13 — now 12 days overdue. The 12 km Beaumonts objective was not attempted. The block served its purpose: tissue tolerance demonstrated at 7+ km (longest run 7.28 km on Sep 5), VO2max running improved 40.6 → 42.3 over the comeback, and gravel cycling has resumed successfully (49.6 km Sep 21). The next block should: (a) consolidate the 5-7 km easy run range at 2 runs/week (matching actual execution cadence), (b) integrate gravel rides as a secondary modality, (c) target the 12 km Beaumonts in a new block once 8-9 km runs are routine. Vitamin D retest remains overdue (last level 27 ng/mL, Dec 2025).
